text:
I passed through the sieve of every sorrow

And I am purified. I cry out for a new life!

A life that will be like a rhythm of silk!

Sweetness and more sweetness! The stillness of an afternoon.


Delightful and sunlit, the little house with ivy

and a patch of sky where the soul tangles itself.


No longing except a child's longing,

to have the swallows of an eternal stillness

and to feel myself so good… so deeply good!…


To read nothing, nothing, except in the lavish,

infinite and precious book of nature

and sip its truths with hope wide open!…


To rise into a new life. To work the miracle

of covering the wound in my veins with jasmine

and making a white song from the remains of tragedy.


To have a heart made of a flash of light,

to have a heart made into a nest of gems

so that other new corollas may always open.


To cross through life with wings in the soul,

with wings in the body, with wings in thought

and a slight fondness for approaching death.


To forgive, forgive, to bear no grudge;

to give everything to oblivion and weep in the quiet

solitude of night with pearly tears.


Pearls of annunciation, of oblivion, of joy,

of sweetness, and the delight of feeling serene

and understanding life as a rhythm of silk.


Today I desire it so… today, a feast day,

and I have much of Christmas Eve within my soul…

translation.title: Rise Again
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the prayerlike infinitives, the recurring silk-rhythm image, and the movement from purification through forgiveness toward renewal. The source contains compressed punctuation in “Purificada.¡Clamo” and “¡tan”; the English restores spacing while retaining the exclamatory force.
